Women 1st Match Sri Lanka tour of Pakistan, 2026 Ghori, Razaullah push Pakistan to commanding position in Rawalpindi
 by Cricbuzz Staff •     Share Tweet Lahiru Kumara took a five-fer but Pakistan still edged ahead. © AFP Lahiru Kumara took a five-fer but Pakistan still edged ahead. © AFP Pakistan tightened their grip on the second Test in Rawalpindi, taking a massive 227-run first-innings lead and then reducing Sri Lanka to 74 for 3 before bad light forced early Stumps on Day 2. Lahiru Kumara’s 5 for 95 helped the visitors put up a fight after being bowled out for a paltry 98 on the opening day, but Ghazi Ghori’s maiden Test fifty and Razaullah’s 32-ball 42 led a late charge that pushed Pakistan’s total to 325.
 Pakistan, who began the day on 121/3, were jolted early when Kumara struck in his second over of the morning, removing Azan Awais on 47 with a pearler that swung away late to catch the outside edge. Nightwatchman Saqib Khan and Saud Shakeel then steadied the innings with a 57-run stand for the fifth wicket, but Kumara struck again to provide the breakthrough, this time with an outside edge to the keeper. 
 Kumara struck again in his next over, removing Saqib with a dipping full toss when the field was set for bouncers. Asitha Fernando then trapped Salman Agha LBW as Pakistan went to Lunch on 221/7, having lost four wickets for 100 runs in the session.
 Sri Lanka kept the pressure on after the break. Asitha removed Aamer Jamal with a short ball angled into the batter as Pakistan slipped to 261/8. The visitors would have hoped to keep the deficit under 200 but Ghori, who had spent much of the morning in defence, went on to 42 with Jamal for the eighth wicket. 
 Razaullah’s arrival at the crease brought quick runs. Even after Sri Lanka took the second new ball, the ninth-wicket stand grew to 56 off just 52 balls as Ghori reached his fifty before edging a slog off Milan Rathnayake for 54. Kumara then completed his five-wicket haul by bowling Razaullah, who had struck four fours and three sixes.
 The pitch had eased considerably by then but Sri Lanka’s top order faltered again. Saqib had Lahiru Udara caught at extra cover before leaving the field with his left boot taped. Razaullah completed that over and in the next, trapped Dinesh Chandimal LBW for a duck, leaving Sri Lanka tottering at 10/2. Kamindu Mendis rode his luck for 16 off 25 before Jamal had him caught at first slip.
 Dhananjaya de Silva and Pasindu Sooriyabandara then saw Sri Lanka through to the close with an unbroken stand of 35 but an uphill task awaits the visitors on the third day, with the deficit still at 153.
 Brief scores : Sri Lanka 98 & 74/3 (Dhananjaya de Silva 24*; Razaullah 1-22, Aamer Jamal 1-16) trail Pakistan 325 (Ghazi Ghori 54; Lahiru Kumara 5-95) by 153 runs.
